entities.summary: Louis de Gonzague, Duke of Nevers was a soldier, governor and statesman during the French Wars of Religion. His father and brother were reigning dukes of Mantua. He came to France in 1549, and fought for Henri II of France during the latter Italian Wars, getting himself captured during the battle of Saint Quentin. Due to his Italian connections he was seen as a useful figure to have as governor of French Piedmont, a post he would hold until Henri III ceded the territory in 1574. In 1565 his patron, Catherine de' Medici secured for him a marriage with the key heiress Henriette de Clèves, elevating him to duke of Nevers and count of Rethel.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As governor of French Piedmont, Louis Gonzaga played a crucial role in maintaining French control over the region until its cession to Spain in 1574. His marriage to Henriette de Clèves elevated him to duke of Nevers and count of Rethel.
